bib.title: Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning

read.skipped: Appendix E worked examples were read only in part (math examples garbled by matrix layout); they are qualitative traces.

question: Can an LLM be trained, using only its own generated data and no teacher or second model, to correct its own mistakes at test time (intrinsic self-correction)?
hypothesis: Offline SFT on self-generated correction traces fails through distribution shift and behavior collapse; on-policy multi-turn RL with a collapse-resistant initialization and a progress reward bonus can instil effective self-correction.
contributions: Analysis showing SFT variants (STaR, Pair-SFT) on self-generated correction traces fail from distribution shift and behavior collapse
SCoRe, a two-stage multi-turn on-policy RL method with reward shaping for self-correction using entirely self-generated data
State-of-the-art intrinsic self-correction on MATH (Gemini 1.5 Flash) and HumanEval (Gemini 1.0 Pro), plus ablations

method.summary: SCoRe fine-tunes a single Gemini model with REINFORCE and a KL penalty over a two-turn rollout (attempt, then a fixed self-correction instruction that does not reveal correctness). Stage I trains second-attempt reward while a strong KL ties first attempts to the base model; Stage II optimises both attempts with a progress bonus alpha*(r2 - r1) on the second attempt.
method.task: intrinsic self-correction for math reasoning (MATH) and code generation (MBPP train, HumanEval test), two attempts, binary correctness reward

datasets.name: MATH
datasets.size: MATH training set plus 4500 test problems for training; 500 problems held out (MATH500)
datasets.split: following Lightman et al. (2023); report on remaining 500 problems
datasets.preprocessing: binary reward: answer matches ground truth

datasets.name: MBPP
datasets.preprocessing: binary reward: passes all test cases; canonical three-shot prompt for first-attempt training samples

datasets.name: HumanEval
datasets.split: evaluation only, test cases not exposed to model

datasets.name: MBPP-R
datasets.split: offline repair task: correct incorrect first-attempt programs generated by PaLM 2

models.name: SCoRe
models.init_from: Gemini 1.5 Flash (MATH), Gemini 1.0 Pro (code); Stage II initialised from Stage I

training.objective: Stage I: max E[r(y2,y*) - beta2*KL(pi(.|x1)||pi_ref(.|x1))] (strict KL on first attempt only, plus small default KL beta1). Stage II: max E[sum_{i=1..2} r(yi,y*) - beta1*KL] with second-attempt reward bonus b = alpha*(r(y2,y*) - r(y1,y*)). REINFORCE with KL penalty (Ahmadian et al., 2024); only instantaneous reward (gamma = 0).
training.regularisation: KL to base model: beta1 = 0.01 (both), beta2 = 0.1 (MATH) / 0.25 (MBPP); reward-shaping alpha = 10 (both)

other.budget: fixed budget of model samples and gradient updates; learning rate and batch size not varied between training methods
other.adaptive_beta2: optionally an adaptive beta2 balancing first-attempt KL against second-attempt objective
other.offline_first_attempts: in some experiments, first-attempt solutions sampled repeatedly from the base model are added as offline prompts in RL, especially Stage II
other.baselines_sft: STaR: 3 iterations (protocol of Singh et al. 2024); Pair-SFT: 1 iteration; data built from Gemini 1.5 Flash two-turn traces on MATH
other.stage_epochs_split: not stated which fraction of 3000 steps is Stage I versus Stage II

inference.decoding: greedy (temperature 0) for all evaluations except inference-compute scaling
inference.samples: one greedy run, two sequential attempts (one round of self-correction); scaling experiment up to 32 solutions per problem with self-consistency
inference.prompting: zero-shot CoT on MATH; zero-shot on HumanEval; canonical three-shot for MBPP first attempts; second attempt uses a self-correction instruction that does not reveal correctness

metrics.name: Accuracy@t2
metrics.definition: accuracy of the second attempt after the self-correction instruction

metrics.name: Delta(t1,t2)
metrics.definition: net accuracy improvement between first and second attempt

metrics.name: Delta i->c(t1,t2)
metrics.definition: fraction of problems incorrect at attempt 1 and correct at attempt 2

metrics.name: Delta c->i(t1,t2)
metrics.definition: fraction of problems correct at attempt 1 and incorrect at attempt 2

metrics.name: MBPP-R
metrics.definition: accuracy at repairing incorrect first-attempt programs from PaLM 2

baselines: STaR D+_STaR (Zelikman et al., 2022; Singh et al.)
Pair-SFT D_SFT (Welleck et al., 2023, single-model variant)
eval.protocol: single run per method; no seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests reported; no majority voting for main results; checkpoint chosen by training reward

results.claim: SCoRe attains a positive intrinsic self-correction delta on MATH (the first significantly positive one), with Accuracy@t2 64.4% against 41.4% for the base model.
results.setup: Gemini 1.5 Flash, MATH500, greedy, one round of self-correction
results.quote: Notably, the intrinsic self-correction gain Δ(t1, t2) of 4.4% is the first significantly positive delta

results.claim: Relative to the base model, SCoRe improves self-correction delta by 15.6% and Accuracy@t2 by 23.0% on MATH.
results.setup: Gemini 1.5 Flash, MATH500, versus base model
results.quote: SCoRe improves Δ(t1, t2) by 15.6%, and Accuracy@t2 by 23.0%

results.claim: SCoRe beats the next best prior approach Pair-SFT by 10.2% in delta and 2.6% in Accuracy@t2 on MATH.
results.quote: over the next best prior approach, Pair-SFT, by 10.2% and 2.6% respectively

results.claim: SCoRe reduces correct-to-incorrect flips from 15.8% (base) to 1.4% on MATH.
results.quote: reduces the proportion of correct answers it changes (15.8% to 1.4%)
results.note: The text says the incorrect-to-correct rate is 14.5% versus 9.5% for base, but Table 2 prints 5.8% (SCoRe) and 4.6% (base) for Delta i->c; the two disagree.

results.claim: Prompting-only Self-Refine gives negative self-correction on MATH.
results.table: Table 2, row Self-Refine (Madaan et al., 2023), column Delta(t1,t2): 52.8% -> 51.8%, -1.0%

results.claim: On HumanEval SCoRe reaches intrinsic self-correction delta of 12.2% with Accuracy@t2 64.6%, versus 3.0% delta for the base model.
results.setup: Gemini 1.0 Pro trained on MBPP only, evaluated on HumanEval
results.quote: achieving a 12.2% intrinsic self-correction delta, or 9% higher than the base model

results.claim: On the offline repair task MBPP-R, SCoRe improves the base model from 47.3% to 60.6%.
results.setup: Gemini 1.0 Pro, repairing PaLM 2 first attempts
results.quote: SCoRe improves the base model from 47.3% to 60.6%

results.claim: Pair-SFT works nearly as well on static MBPP-R (59.8%) but degrades the base model in the self-correction setting on HumanEval (delta -1.8%).
results.note: Text: 'Pair-SFT works nearly as well on the static repair task MBPP-R, but actually degrades the base model when evaluated in the self-correction setting'.

results.claim: Base Gemini 1.5 Flash self-correction on MATH is negative (accuracy drops from 52.6% to 41.4%).
results.setup: Gemini 1.5 Flash with self-correction instruction, MATH500
results.table: Table 1, row Base model, column Delta(t1,t2)

results.claim: Pair-SFT gives only a 1.8% self-correction gain on MATH; it mainly reduces correct-to-incorrect flips.
results.quote: there is only little benefit to self-correction (1.8% gain)

results.claim: STaR with correct-to-correct data (D+_STaR) changes delta by only 0.4% on MATH.
results.setup: Gemini 1.5 Flash, STaR 3 iterations; -14.2% is STaR on D_STaR without correct-to-correct data

results.claim: Ablation: removing Stage I lowers delta to 2.2% and Accuracy@t2 to 61.4%.
results.table: Table 4, row w/o Stage I, column Delta(t1, t2)
results.note: Text: 'without it, the model achieves 2% lower delta and 3% lower accuracy@t2'.

results.table: Table 4, row w/o reward shaping, column Delta(t1, t2)

results.claim: Ablation: single-turn RL training raises Accuracy@t1 (61.8%) but gives negative delta -2.4%.
results.table: Table 4, row w/o multi-turn training, column Delta(t1, t2)

results.claim: At a 32-solution budget, parallel majority voting gains 7.4% accuracy while K parallel samples plus one round of sequential self-correction gains 10.5%.
results.setup: SCoRe on MATH, temperature 0.7, 32 solution budget per problem
results.quote: parallel sampling shows a 7.4% accuracy gain, while combining it with sequential sampling using self-correction yields a 10.5% improvement

results.claim: Over 10 attempts, base model never surpasses its first attempt and Pair-SFT does not improve past attempt two, while SCoRe rises slightly then plateaus.
results.setup: Gemini 1.5 Flash, trained on two attempts only; read from Fig 8
results.note: Qualitative, from Fig 8 and appendix text.

results.claim: Standard multi-turn RL with discount gamma = 0.8 and alpha = 1.0 still collapses to non-correcting behavior.
results.setup: Training accuracy curves on MATH, Fig 9
results.note: Qualitative; no number besides gamma and alpha settings.

limits: Authors did not train for more than one round (two attempts) of self-correction for infrastructure reasons; later rounds may be less effective.
Requires two separate runs (Stage I then Stage II); unifying them is left to future work.
Assumes an oracle reward (answer checker or test cases) during training; no oracle at test time.
Only two Gemini models and two domains (MATH, MBPP/HumanEval); no seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests; checkpoint selected by training reward.
Model sizes, compute, hardware and wall-clock are not stated; code and weights are not released (Gemini models are proprietary).
Text and Table 2 disagree on incorrect-to-correct rates (14.5% vs 9.5% in text; 5.8% vs 4.6% in table).
